Forcing Nepali families back to a home that no longer exists is cruel. We need to act now.

To learn more, visit: https://t.co/BJOYsGdfv0

text:
These latest admissions by Acting Secretary of the Navy Cao that eight sailors assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group attempted suicide during this deployment are deeply troubling. My heart is with these sailors, their families, and every service member who has endured the extraordinary strain of this prolonged deployment.

For months, I have been raising concerns about the conditions aboard the USS Lincoln, including inadequate living conditions, insufficient mental health support, and the overall toll this extended deployment has taken on our service members and their families. These latest revelations underscore the urgent need for answers and accountability.

That is why I led a letter to Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Cao demanding answers about the conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. I also joined my San Diego colleagues in calling for an independent investigation by the Department of Defense Inspector General. We need to understand how conditions deteriorated to this point, whether our service members received the care and support they needed, and what steps the Navy is taking to ensure this never happens again. Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao have yet to respond to either letter.

Our Marines and Sailors have sacrificed so much in service to our country. We owe them more than our gratitude. We owe them the care, support, and resources they need, both during their deployment and when they return home.
https://t.co/5lmkjYk9u2

text:
Since its establishment in 1999, the Office of the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues (SEHI) has been the only office in the federal government solely devoted to pursuing justice for Holocaust survivors and advocating on their behalf. For decades, SEHI has worked with foreign governments, international institutions, and Jewish organizations to pursue restitution and compensation for survivors and their families, recover Nazi-looted property, preserve Holocaust memory, and address unresolved Holocaust-era obligations.

As the number of living Holocaust survivors continues to decline, this work is only becoming more urgent, amplifying the need to appoint a career official as the next SEHI, with the seniority, diplomatic experience, and specialized expertise necessary to negotiate complex restitution and compensation matters. I was proud to work with @RepNadler and members of the Congressional Jewish Caucus to urge Secretary Rubio to preserve the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues position as a distinct and permanent office. This work is too important to be consolidated or eliminated, and we will continue to fight for the pursuit of justice on behalf of Holocaust survivors and their families.

Faith has always been part of my life since my upbringing.

Our church is where I learned Bible verses, attended Sunday School, and Vacation Bible School. It’s where I often got my brand-new Easter suits dirty looking for eggs, learned the Apostles’ Creed and about the fruit of the Spirit, and was baptized. It’s also where I declared Jesus as my Savior, and this foundation still guides me today. 

Proverbs 22:6, “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.”

RT @IATSE: IATSE Lauds Introduction of Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, Urges Swift Passage

WASHINGTON, D…

reposted.text:
IATSE Lauds Introduction of Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, Urges Swift Passage

WASHINGTON, D.C. — The International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) today applauded the introduction of the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act (MPTERA), which would create a federal incentive to level the playing field and bring film and television jobs back to the United States. 

The bill follows years of IATSE advocacy for a competitive, labor-based federal production incentive.

The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act would:

Provide a 20% base tax credit on qualified compensation for qualified film and television productions. 

- Eligible productions include feature films, television pilots, and television seasons with total costs above $1 million and at least 75% of principal photography days occur within the United States.
- Qualified compensation is defined as payments for labor-based services (including pre-production, and post-production work) performed in the United States.

Provide a 20% base credit for qualifying traditional post-production and visual effects work when at least 75% of the total costs for the respective VFX and TPP services are incurred in the United States.

Offer bonus credits of 5%, up to a maximum total credit of 30%, for productions that meet specified domestic investment requirements. Productions could qualify for bonus credits by:
- Filming in a rural qualified opportunity zone or federally declared disaster area.
- Meeting the bill’s requirements for qualifying as an independent production.
- Conducting at least 50% of principal photography in 10 or more states, with at least $10,000,000 in qualified compensation.
- Taxpayers who increase their number of domestic productions relative to a historical foreign base amount

“The over 170,000 behind-the-scenes entertainment workers of the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) are proud to endorse the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act,” said International President Matthew D. Loeb. “IATSE has long called for a globally competitive, labor-based federal production incentive to level the playing field for American workers, return middle-class film and television jobs to America, and keep them here at home.

“This legislation would achieve that goal, addressing the dramatic loss of tens of thousands of American jobs in motion picture production and post-production. IATSE praises Senators Scott and Schiff, and Representatives Moran, Sanchez, Jack, Friedman, Carey, Chu, Kustoff, and Suozzi for leading this bipartisan effort. IATSE calls on all members of Congress to support and pass this critical jobs bill before the end of the year,” Loeb continued.

Swift passage of this bill is IATSE’s foremost federal legislative priority, as it would be transformative for our members’ future work opportunities and economic well-being after years of scarcity. We urge all members of Congress to cosponsor this legislation and push for it to become law.

text:
Today, I’m announcing the conclusion and findings of an independent investigation into allegations regarding Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell. The investigation found that the Lieutenant Governor engaged in serious, repeated violations of state policy and failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office. I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so. 

I hold everyone in my Administration to the highest ethical standard. We all have a duty to follow our state ethics and harassment policy and our Code of Conduct. Anyone who violates these will be held accountable.

These violations substantiated in the investigation reflect a pattern of behavior that does not meet the standards of this Administration. The ethical lapses persisted despite multiple warnings and trainings. The substantiated finding of sexual harassment is extremely troubling. I’ve seen firsthand how a hostile culture can undermine everyone’s ability to succeed. It’s insidious and ruptures the trust within an organization.

Leaders have an obligation to make sure everyone in an organization is bought into the mission and able to succeed. I take that responsibility incredibly seriously. My goal as Governor is to empower our hardworking public servants, so they can remain focused on serving our state.

As a former federal prosecutor, I’m committed to ensuring everyone is treated fairly. This investigation was thorough and impartial. It was initiated by the Chief Ethics Officer and conducted by a respected former state Attorney General.

The investigation fully examined the evidence, followed the facts, and protected everyone’s privacy. In my Administration, we are committed to doing what is right, not what is politically expedient.

The Lieutenant Governor’s resignation is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents.

The President continues to undermine confidence in public service at the federal level. In New Jersey, I will not accept a culture that sweeps misconduct under the rug. We have to be better than that — people expect and deserve better.

I have dedicated my life to service. I know that jobs of public trust impact the lives of everyday people, and I deeply respect the oaths and responsibilities of these positions.

I will always put the interests of the people of New Jersey first.

text:
Hello right wingers. Yes, this person reached out to me. No, we haven't opened a case. If the person in question lives outside the district, we refer it to their Member of Congress. 

I'm easy to reach, so I get messages like this all the time from every community: white, black, brown, etc. I help everyone. 

Also, I'm American. Born here, never lived anywhere else. My skin color, being of Asian descent, or practicing a particular religion doesn't make me any less American. Think about that when you call on me to be deported.

quoted.text:
I was passed these messages from a private Tamil community group. I removed the identity of the H-1B worker because this is not about attacking him.

Instead, look at what happened around him. First, he develops an immigration problem after losing his job. Next, someone in the group asks whether they can “steer some help” through Congressman Suhas Subramanyam’s office.

Another member says he had just met Subramanyam at an event and could arrange a call. Then, within the same conversation: “I reached out to Suhas and emailed him and forwarded to his immigration team.” — “Connecting his family to Suhas in the morning.”

You may have missed it, but the messages say the worker lives in Herndon. Herndon in Virginia’s 11th Congressional District. Subramanyam represents the 10th District.  

House Ethics guidance says members generally should not devote official resources to casework for people outside their district and can instead refer them to their own representative or senators.  

I don’t think Subramanyam was summoned based on the district he represents. 

Remember, this conversation is taking place inside a Tamil community network. So, it’s worth noting that Subramanyam has South Indian family roots, his father grew up in Chennai and he was a congressional co-sponsor of the resolution recognizing Tamil Language and Heritage Month.  

Sure, we don’t have proof of preferential treatment or what his office ultimately did. But we did get an unusually candid look at how political access in ethnic networks functions:

Private ethnic community → personal connection → member of Congress → congressional immigration team.

Despite being unable to vote and being out of district, people around him apparently knew exactly who to contact and claimed the personal access to get his case in front of a congressional office.

The question I want answered is simple: why was this case being routed through Suhas Subramanyam and what did his office do with it?

When you cut funds and jobs at the FDA, it's not a question of if people will get sick; it's a question of when. And since 2025, it has been all the time. 

When Democrats win big in November, we will bring back accountability and transparency. This isn't a red or blue issue. Our food should be safe to eat; it's really that simple.

text:
I welcome Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 American students to visit and study in China.   As Co-Chair of the Congressional International Exchanges Caucus, I believe educational and cultural exchanges are an important way to build mutual understanding and expertise.  But those exchanges depend on trust and the ability to study, speak, and engage without fear of harassment or arbitrary detention. 

Right now, American scholar Min Zin remains wrongfully detained in China, and Beijing continues to target scholars, human rights advocates, and diaspora communities whose work or speech it finds unwelcome.   If President Xi wants more Americans to study in China, releasing Min Zin would be an important first step toward creating the conditions that make genuine cultural and educational exchange possible between our two nations.
